cases.why: Season Accuracy carries the same h3 twice, so the page reads as though it repeats itself and the heading stops identifying a section. This happened for real: rewriting two related sections in plain English converged on the same short question, which is exactly how it recurs. This case ALSO proves the heading scan reads render-function output and not just page markup -- the heading it mutates is emitted from a JavaScript template literal, so a markup-only scan would let this survive, which is what the first draft of the guard did

the landing page goes back to explaining itself in statistics vocabulary. Re-anchored 2026-09-15: this used to mutate the page's standfirst paragraph, which was deleted in a declutter pass, and the SOS note is now the longest piece of prose a casual reader meets on Power Ratings. The lesson is the reason it was re-anchored rather than dropped -- deleting the only input that reaches a branch silently untests the branch, and this page is the guard's most important page precisely because it is the one that loads first.
